summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) as the authoritative DNS resolver for the LAN shared with node2 and node3 (Ubuntu 16.04). Unbound on node1 resolves normal names recursively, but has a DNSBL wildcard blocklist entry for blocked.example (and all subdomains) with rcode=NXDOMAIN, so that domain and everything under it resolves to nothing usable. node2 and node3 were repointed to use node1 (10.100.44.10) as their sole nameserver via systemd-networkd DNS= plus a static /etc/resolv.conf (networkd's DHCP-derived resolver kept leaking into resolvconf despite UseDNS=no, so a static resolv.conf was used for reliable persistence). Verified normal resolution (google.com, example.com) works from both hosts while blocked.example/sub.blocked.example fail (NXDOMAIN / getent exit 2). Performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot identities, issued native reboot, polled until each node's control channel returned, confirmed the boot identity changed on every node, and reverified DNS resolution/blocking end-to-end after each restart before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: OPNsense (FreeBSD 14.3) appliance running Unbound (port 53, primary resolver) and dnsmasq (port 53053)
Inspected node2/node3: Ubuntu 16.04 hosts using systemd-networkd v229 + resolvconf, originally pointed at platform gateway 10.100.44.1 instead of node1
Edited node1's /conf/config.xml via a Python ElementTree script to add an Unbound DNSBL blocklist entry: wildcards=blocked.example, nxdomain=1, enabled=1
Regenerated Unbound templates (configctl template reload 'OPNsense/Unbound/*'), ran configctl unbound dnsbl to build the blocklist, and configctl unbound restart to apply
Verified locally on node1 and remotely from node2/node3 that google.com/example.com resolve normally while blocked.example and sub.blocked.example/deep.sub.blocked.example return NXDOMAIN
Edited /etc/systemd/network/50-antrieb-dhcp.network on node2 and node3 to add DNS=10.100.44.10 and [DHCP] UseDNS=no

Replaced the resolvconf-managed symlink /etc/resolv.conf on node2 and node3 with a static file pointing solely at nameserver 10.100.44.10, since networkd continued writing the DHCP-supplied 10.100.44.1 into the resolvconf hook file despite UseDNS=no
Captured baseline boot identities: node1 kern.boottime (17:36:12), node2 boot_id 2ba78175..., node3 boot_id f6f9440e...

Restarted node1 via shutdown -r +0, polled until SSH/exec returned, confirmed kern.boottime changed to 17:47:36, and reverified Unbound service, normal resolution, and blocked.example NXDOMAIN both locally and from node2

Restarted node2 via sudo shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed to 50ed94f0..., and reverified static resolv.conf, normal resolution, and blocked domain failure (getent exit 2)

Restarted node3 via sudo shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed to 34e7ebdf..., and reverified static resolv.conf, normal resolution, and blocked domain failure for both blocked.example and sub.blocked.example
Final cross-check on node1 post all-node restarts confirmed unbound/dnsmasq processes running and DNS blocking still functioning

evidence.requirement: node1 provides working name resolution for normal domains to node2 and node3
evidence.summary: Unbound on node1 resolves google.com/example.com; node2 and node3 querying node1 directly and via their default resolver get correct A records

evidence.requirement: blocked.example and all subdomains resolve to nothing usable from both node2 and node3
evidence.summary: DNSBL wildcard block (nxdomain=1) on node1 causes blocked.example, sub.blocked.example, and deep.sub.blocked.example to return NXDOMAIN; getent hosts exits 2 (host not found) on both client nodes

evidence.requirement: DNSBL blocklist configuration applied and persisted in node1 config.xml, DNS service reconfigured
evidence.summary: config.xml edited with dnsbl blocklist entry, Unbound templates regenerated, blocklist built and unbound restarted to apply

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to use node1 as their DNS server persistently
evidence.summary: systemd-networkd DNS= set and static /etc/resolv.conf pointing only at 10.100.44.10 written on both nodes, confirmed effective and immune to resolvconf/networkd regeneration

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline boot identity and health before restart
evidence.summary: kern.boottime captured as 1788629772 (17:36:12); unbound/dnsmasq running; google.com resolves, blocked.example NXDOMAIN

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: shutdown -r issued and acknowledged; exec connection timed out during reboot; kern.boottime changed to 1788630456 (17:47:36); unbound/dnsmasq confirmed running post-boot; DNS resolution and blocking verified locally and from node2

evidence.summary: boot_id captured as f6f9440e-50f4-4050-b430-17b1e838eadf, uptime since 13:36:12

evidence.summary: reboot issued (connection closed as expected); exec refused during reboot; boot_id changed to 34e7ebdf-03d2-4ceb-b837-bebba48395da; static resolv.conf intact, google.com resolves, blocked.example and sub.blocked.example fail with getent exit 2
